posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
Cristiano, when making a Denisyuk, try to lay the plate horizontally right on the object. Choose an object that has three points the plate can lay on. Most vibrations will not ruin this type of set up. You can then remove the interferometer and use the additional power. Use the least amount of optics also. You can then expand your beam more to remove the hot spot without increasing the exposure time too much. In fact I would not be surprised if you can go to 10 minutes with this set up and still have no movement.

When I shoot Denisyuks with the above geometry, even though I shoot for about 1 minute, I keep the music playing, I walk around, the water is running there are no worries about vibrations. I think I read on the .it forum that you use tire tubes for vibration dampening. If so, I believe not even the train will cause movement if you lay the plate right on the object.

Keep up the great work. Your holograms looks fantastic.

If so, I'm somewhat surprised by the exposure time needed. Is the 20mW laser actually putting out 20mW or is that the "rated" amount?

20 mW is the actual optical power, less a couple of mW used by the interferometer.

> **dave battin:** Cristiano,Geat hologram, its nice to see you are making your own film pates ! many on this forum claim to make thier own film (and few will post pictures)......what method of coating are you using ? is it possible you have a varing sensitivity across the plate?

I think making own plates is a quite laborious job, but very exciting and satisfactory.

The coating method is well decribed in the Wiki by Hans. I tried with other methods but since at this moment I can't use a laminar flow hood, I prefere the easy way.

Finally, I don't know if sesistivity is constant across the plate, I suppose (and assume) yes. Color shift is present only changing the reference beam. Please note that the photo were shot using a sodium yellow light as reference light. Furthermore, I didn't use a spatial filter for this setup.
